answer: A crystal can be read once and forgotten; a life cannot. Once per epoch the ledger picks a dated entry from the account's own history and asks the holder to reproduce a private detail from it. Aged identities answer from memory at zero cost; a hollow ring of clones has no real past to recall and must script thousands of personalized quizzes or stall. Peers simply check each answer against the atlas of recorded dates, so a fabricated reply is visible to everyone forever.
